instruction: Navigate to the desktop settings and enable the automatic screen lock feature.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.explanation: Task requires enabling automatic screen lock via desktop settings. Initial config sets lock-enabled to false. Agent must navigate settings and enable it. Evaluator verifies lock-enabled is true.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly verifies the screen lock setting using gsettings command-line tool
Complete coverage: instruction requires enabling automatic screen lock, evaluator checks lock-enabled setting is true
Getter logic is correct: get_vm_command_line (general.py:8) executes 'gsettings get org.gnome.desktop.screensaver lock-enabled' and returns stdout
Metric logic is correct: exact_match (general.py:41) performs string equality comparison between result and expected
Expected value is semantically correct: 'true\n' matches exact gsettings output format (includes trailing newline)
Data flow is sound: gsettings command → string output 'true\n' → exact_match comparison → returns 1.0 if enabled, 0.0 otherwise
Static warning is false positive: verification uses command-line gsettings (not UI state inspection), so postconfig to close Settings window does not affect verification
Practical and feasible: gsettings is standard GNOME configuration tool, always accessible via command line regardless of UI state or window focus
No edge case issues: gsettings command will work even if Settings app crashes or is closed during verification
